---
title: "Sources and licences"
---

Transcription starts with somebody else's artifact, which makes source keeping a
musical problem as well as a legal one. The exact edition or recording you
worked from decides what you can inspect, what you can share, and where you go
back to when two details disagree. This ledger records that provenance, and
Lesson 42 walks you through one entry before any external file lands in your
repository.

Public-domain status differs by country. A modern typeset edition of an old work
carries rights of its own even when the composition underneath it is free to
use. So the composer's death date opens the question. Your exact edition and
recording are what close it.

## What the first draft ships

This draft distributes no third-party score, MIDI file, or recording. Its
manuscript, Sonic Pi examples, and exercise melodies were generated by GPT 5.6
Sol at High Reasoning. They're under revision and independent testing, and no
human-authored edition is claimed.

| Material | Draft creator | Source | Used in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lesson prose and original exercise melodies | GPT 5.6 Sol at High Reasoning | This repository | Throughout |
| Sonic Pi code examples | GPT 5.6 Sol at High Reasoning | This repository | Throughout |
| Musical Equalizer icon | Gauden Galea | `assets/img/favicon.png` | Site and book identity |

When an exercise asks you to choose a public-domain source, your choosing it
changes nothing about the rights on that external artifact. Your copy stays
governed by its own edition, performance, and recording terms.

## Where to look

| Source | What it holds | Watch for |
|---|---|---|
| [IMSLP](https://imslp.org/) | Scanned scores and parts from many periods | Item status, edition rights, and permitted use vary by jurisdiction |
| [Mutopia](https://www.mutopiaproject.org/) | Typeset scores offered with item-level terms | Verify the displayed terms and the source edition |
| [MuseScore](https://musescore.com/) | Community scores and arrangements | Access and rights vary per upload; an available score is not automatic permission to redistribute |

These links help you find material. They don't grant you permission for any
particular item, so save the item page, the file, and the licence statement
together. Availability and national public-domain rules move independently of
each other. IMSLP's own [public-domain
guidance](https://imslp.org/wiki/Public_domain) says as much: status varies
between countries, and the site doesn't guarantee that its general information
is legally accurate for the use you have in mind.

## Record one item

Use one row per exact artifact. "Bach minuet" won't do, because the composition,
the typesetting, the edition, the performance, and the recording can each belong
to a different rightsholder.

| Field | Record |
|---|---|
| Piece | Work title and catalogue number where one exists |
| Composer | Name plus death year used for the public-domain check |
| Source | Stable page address, archive identifier, or repository path |
| Edition | Editor, publisher, date, and scan or typeset identifier |
| Performance | Performer and recording date if audio is used |
| Licence | Exact licence or public-domain mark shown by the source |
| Retrieved | Date the artifact and its rights statement were saved |
| Used in | Lesson and measure or time range |

When a judgement went into an entry, keep a local note beside the artifact. A
useful note states the rule you applied and the evidence you checked. It should
not claim that the same rule holds in every country, because you have no way of
knowing that.

## Candidate-source worksheet

The transcription chapters ask you to pick short material yourself, so there's
no universal piece to name here. Add a row before you bring an external artifact
into a published edition.

| Piece | Composer | Source | Edition or recording | Licence evidence | Intended lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reader-selected four-bar melody | To be recorded by the reader | Local copy | Exact artifact required | Verify before redistribution | 41-46 |

That placeholder row describes a workflow, not a licensed asset. Replace it once
you have the chosen artifact and its evidence in hand.

## Repository rule

Don't commit an external score or recording because its composition is old.
Commit it when the exact artifact has an entry above, the licence permits this
form of redistribution, and the attribution sits beside every use. Links die
too, so keep the retrieval date and enough metadata to find another lawful copy.

For material that stays on your own machine, cite the source in your field notes
and leave the file out of the repository. Watch one thing here: the code
representation you build from a work can still encode a substantial part of it.
Publishing that representation is its own rights decision, and you should treat
it as one.
